synthesis: Kit Path Map (the client-portal Filament page 'Kit User Path', rendering through KitUserPathController::paths()) today draws each kit's route from a two-tier ClickHouse pipeline. Tier 1 assembles a continuous-GPS route from clarity.sc_positions via KitRangePathsQuery and runs unconditionally for every kit with a non-empty kit_mapping. Tier 2 builds a scan-derived polyline from clarity.kit_scan_paths via KitScanPathsQuery, but only for kits with zero tier-1 coverage anywhere in the selected window. That tier-1-primary arrangement is the deliberate, hardened outcome of DEV-2177 (built the continuous route precisely because scan-only looked fragmented), DEV-2374 (bbox pushdown, budget), and DEV-2441 (the tier-2 fallback), the last of which merged on 2026-08-28 -- three days before this branch was cut. DEV-2451 asks for scan data only, in the interim, until enriched kit/SC_POSITIONS work lands (linked as DEV-2450). The ticket is genuinely ambiguous between (A) actively gating tier 1 off, which reverts a just-shipped feature and deliberately reintroduces the fragmented-route UX DEV-2177 existed to fix, for 617 kits that currently render continuous routes; and (B) a near no-op plus documentation, on the reading that 'merged GL/SC_POSITIONS' means an enrichment source that does not exist yet, so nothing depends on it today. Both readings are defensible from the ticket text; the code cannot settle it. All four independent prep passes reached this same conclusion and all four declined to answer it.

questions.q: Does 'use scan data only' mean actively gating OFF the tier-1 continuous-GPS route (KitRangePathsQuery / clarity.sc_positions) that DEV-2441 shipped three days ago -- moving all 617 currently-GPS-rendering kits onto the more fragmented kit_scan_paths view -- or does 'merged GL/SC_POSITIONS data' mean an enrichment source that does not exist yet, making this a documentation-only ticket? Reading A reverts just-shipped, heavily-reviewed work and visibly degrades route fidelity; reading B changes no behavior. The two produce opposite diffs.

questions.q: Is kit_scan_paths the right scan-derived source, and does it need a new query class?
questions.answer: Yes and no respectively. clarity.kit_scan_paths is scan-derived (path_points from the scan tables, distinct producer from sc_positions) and KitScanPathsQuery::encodedPaths() already emits the exact wire shape tier 1 does. Under reading A the change is pure routing -- no new query class, no new data source, no frontend change.

questions.q: Would gating tier 1 off risk a resource blow-up on kit_scan_paths?
questions.answer: Unlikely -- the direction is favorable. Gating tier 1 off REMOVES the expensive sc_positions decimation/segmentation assembly (PG-022: the read that needed bbox pushdown to get a 200-kit/7-day selection from ~1GB refused down to ~20MB), and the shared MAX_RENDER_POINTS=1,500,000 budget still backstops tier 2. Measured: kit_scan_paths is only 1.66M rows total fleet-wide. The real risk is UX regression scope, not exhaustion.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT uniqExact(kit_id), uniqExact(org_id) FROM clarity.kit_scan_paths WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL <N> DAY
derivation_log.why: Sizes the tier-2 population that becomes the sole source under reading A.
Confirms tier 2 is small (1.66M) relative to the 1.5M render-point budget, so the envelope direction is favourable. Matches DEV-2441's ~1.68M.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT uniqExact(lower(kit_mapping)) FROM clarity.sc_positions WHERE timestamp_utc >= now() - INTERVAL <N> DAY
derivation_log.why: THE regression-scope number: how many kits currently render a continuous route and would degrade under reading A. Cross-validates DEV-2441's '610 GPS kits / 494 newly render'.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT count(), countIf(gl IS NOT NULL), uniqExact(gl) FROM clarity.sc_positions WHERE timestamp_utc >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 136527018 rows, 0 null gl, 469 distinct gl values; column type String
derivation_log.why: Establishes that the ticket's 'merged GL' names a real, fully-populated column rather than a hypothetical future source -- which is why the premise is imprecise rather than false.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT countIf(n>1), count(), max(n) FROM (SELECT gl, uniqExact(lower(kit_mapping)) AS n FROM clarity.sc_positions WHERE <window> GROUP BY gl)
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 454 of 469 gl values map to >1 kit_mapping; worst fan-out 11
derivation_log.why: Tests whether GL->kit attribution is clean. It is not -- but this direction is irrelevant to tier 1, which keys on kit_mapping.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT countIf(n>1), count(), max(n), quantile(0.95)(n) FROM (SELECT lower(kit_mapping) AS km, uniqExact(gl) AS n FROM clarity.sc_positions WHERE <window> AND trim(kit_mapping) != '' GROUP BY km)
derivation_log.param_classes: window length in days; blank-mapping exclusion
derivation_log.aggregate_result: Including blanks: 165/617 mappings carry >1 gl, worst 467. EXCLUDING blanks: 164/616, worst 6, p95 3.
derivation_log.why: The alarming 467 fan-out is entirely on the BLANK kit_mapping sentinel, which tier 1 already excludes via mappingIndex(). Among real mappings the worst case is 6 gl values over 30 days -- fully consistent with scanner hardware swaps. So this is NOT evidence of a live tier-1 misattribution defect.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT countIf(trim(kit_mapping) = ''), count() FROM clarity.sc_positions WHERE <window>
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 19043981 of 136531089 rows (14%) carry a blank kit_mapping
derivation_log.why: Quantifies the sentinel population that tier 1 discards -- context for the fan-out finding above.
